rules.statement: Don't add a server-sent-events or WebSocket endpoint, or a shared-state pub/sub primitive, to a BFF to push session-ended events to open tabs; the 401 of the next guarded call is the signal.
rules.why: Each push stream holds one of the six HTTP/1.1 connections per origin and starves the application. It also needs cross-replica pub/sub and connection bounds, and EventSource cannot send the anti-forgery header. A push only changes how soon a stale page clears.
rules.check: Look for new MapGet endpoints returning text/event-stream, WebSocket middleware or endpoints, or new pub/sub primitives in a BFF meant to notify about session end or logout.

rules.statement: A BFF guarded API call or user-info endpoint reached without a live session must answer 401 with the session_required problem type, never a redirect.
rules.why: The 401 problem response is the single signal frontends rely on to learn a session ended. It holds on every replica, whichever way the session ended.
rules.check: Check how guarded BFF endpoints handle a missing or expired session: flag a redirect or challenge to login, a 403, or a 401 without the session_required problem type.

rules.statement: A BFF's user/session-info endpoint (such as GET /bff/user) must only read the session and never slide its idle expiration window.
rules.why: Frontends poll this endpoint to detect the end of a session, so a poll must not keep the session alive.
rules.check: Look for the user-info endpoint renewing, touching or refreshing the session's idle expiry, or the cookie sliding on that path.

rules.statement: A BFF's user/session-info endpoint must return the session's idle expiry and absolute expiry times so frontends can probe when they pass.
rules.why: Frontends schedule probes at session.idleExpiresAt and session.expiresAt and reread them after every answer.
rules.check: Check that changes to the user-info response keep the idle and absolute expiry fields and don't remove or rename them.

rules.statement: Frontend code behind a BFF that detects a session end (a 401 session_required or a logout) must broadcast it to its other tabs through a BroadcastChannel and send the user to the BFF's login, directly or through a sign-in screen whose click starts it.
rules.why: Sharing one tab's answer clears every tab. On its own, BroadcastChannel never learns of a back-channel logout, an idle timeout or a failed refresh, so it supplements the poll and doesn't replace it.
rules.check: In frontend session handling, look for a 401 or logout handler that doesn't notify other tabs, or one that relies only on BroadcastChannel without handling 401 or probing.

rules.statement: Frontend code that polls or probes BFF session state must send the anti-forgery header and recheck on visibilitychange when a hidden tab becomes visible.
rules.why: The user-info endpoint is guarded by the anti-forgery header, and browsers throttle a hidden tab's timers, so scheduled probes may not have run.
rules.check: In frontend polling of the BFF user endpoint, look for missing anti-forgery headers or a missing visibilitychange recheck.
